mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months, or signal fails to outperform random walk in 3-year backtests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL above 2.5% and decline in FEDFUNDS below 0.1% indicates policy response to inflation, preceding positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as markets anticipate accommodative measures.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS conditions, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 1.5% for three consecutive months), higher discount rates and reduced liquidity cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5% for three months, or signal's predictive power is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring specific thresholds.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST rises, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, it indicates manufacturing slowdown that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to recession fears.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100 for two months, or signal's predictive accuracy is not significantly better than random (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE signals labor market deterioration that precedes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or interaction term is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) fall below 540,000 million dollars for two consecutive months, it indicates weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS falls below 540,000 for two months, or signal's Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.
